note: Transcribed from the actual sequence of tune.py/ablate.py runs performed during development (see reconfigured/README.md for the narrative and log excerpts) rather than a single end-to-end main() invocation -- main() documents the intended reproducible methodology (cross_validate() + fit_final()), but re-running all of it from scratch (2 CV folds + 9 full-data seeds, each a 1500-trial random search + 3-pass coordinate ascent over 71-142 images) takes several hours. Re-running main() will reproduce results in the same range but not bit-identical ones, since random_search's seeding is deterministic per-call but the exact seed/BOUNDS history below reflects what was actually run.

ablation_decast_atlas_fix.description: Isolated test (reconfigured/ablate.py) of the decast-atlas fix ANALYSIS.md proposed, using giacomo's ORIGINAL weights (SIFT disabled) so only the reference-model change varies. Both variants also include the two confirmed-good fixes (aspect-preserving crop_disc, data-derived offdiag).
ablation_decast_atlas_fix.conclusion: Decasting the atlas-building crop made things worse (49.30% -> 45.77%): REF_EDGE's per-class Canny thresholds were implicitly calibrated against the raw photo's contrast. Reverted; the shipped reference.py builds the atlas from the raw reference photo, same as giacomo/tiziano, and keeps only the aspect-crop + offdiag fixes at this layer.

cross_validation.description: Two-fold CV (odd/even target-image split, mirroring giacomo's own dev/sealed convention), fit on the corrected reference model (decast-atlas fix reverted). This is the honest generalization estimate: the weights were never fit against the fold they're measured on. Widened BOUNDS (as shipped in tune.py).

earlier_run_narrower_bounds_for_referenc.description: Before BOUNDS was widened (FAM_POS lower bound 0.5 instead of 0.1, etc.), the same two-fold CV gave a slightly higher held-out estimate. Kept here for transparency about search variance across seeds/bounds.

cross_validation.conclusion: Honest expected generalization for the tuned reconfigured pipeline is roughly 48-51% amount accuracy -- a modest, real improvement over giacomo's 48.59%, not a dramatic one. Train/val gaps (e.g. 64.8% train vs 47.9% val in fold A) show real overfitting risk from 18 free parameters fit against 71 images; treat any single run's exact number as noisy within a few points.

final_full_data_fit.description: The weights actually shipped in reconfigured/config.py: fit on the FULL 142-image set (no held-out fold, since this is the deployed calibration, same practice as giacomo's own notebook-tuned constants). This is an IN-SAMPLE fit -- expect real-world performance closer to the cross-validated estimate above, not this number.
final_full_data_fit.picked_by: lowest mean_abs_err across seeds tried (the search's actual optimization objective, to avoid metric-shopping by amount_acc post-hoc)

notable_finding: Both independent CV fold fits (A and B, different train data, different random seeds) drove FAM_POS down to near the search's lower bound on their own -- a consistent signal, not overfitting noise, that giacomo's original FAM_POS=3.4 over-weights the colour/family cue once the aspect-crop and offdiag fixes are in place.
